title: Rollout snackpack: quickstart & release minimap (Oct 2026 draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact field-ready checklist + hour-by-hour minimap for a small-to-medium release lane. This snackpack is intended for short (<= 36h) rollouts where we want a tightly scoped canary, quick telemetry validation, and a clear rollback ladder. Keep it simple: operator-friendly commands, explicit smoke samples, and one-page escalation cues.

Scope / when to use:
- Feature releases, performance tuning, model swap-ins for hosted API routes.
- NOT for infra-wide migrations, DB schema changes, or multi-region capacity moves.

Owners & communication:
- Release lead: Aisha Patel (on-call lead for the rollout window)
- Ops liaison: Diego Morales (pager)
- SRE backup: Rina Sato (30m response SLA during watch)
- Communications: Connor Blake (customer comms + status page)
- Slack channel: #release-snackpack (create 2h before go-time)

Preflight checklist (must green before starting):
- [ ] Branch merged and CI green, all tests passed (unit + smoke). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482
- [ ] Canary config uploaded to deploy system and verified (percent rollout, target route)
- [ ] Model artifact checksum validated and pinned in manifest (sha256 tagged)
- [ ] Deployment bundle uploaded to staging registry and can be pulled from prod nodes
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards copied to live watchboard (latency, error-rate, token-throughput)
- [ ] Pager duty rota set and on-call acknowledgements recorded
- [ ] Customer-impact matrix reviewed; customers flagged for potential brief window outages notified by Communications
- [ ] Night/Weekend exemption approved (if applicable)

Rollout minimap (36h window recommended; adjust percent ramps for shorter windows):
T-2h: final smoke-run in staging with production-sized payload. Verify KV cache warm path.
T-30m: create Slack channel, post rollout checklist + escalation ladder. Notify SRE and CS.
T-10m: set maintenance flag on non-critical telemetry aggregators (to reduce noise)
T+0: start canary at 1% traffic (5–10 minute steady state)
T+10m: run automated canary smoke suite (see smoke test snippets below)
T+20m: if no regression, move to 5% traffic
T+40m: telemetry check; if stable, 20% traffic
T+1h30m: full-step to 50% if stable; hold for 1h
T+2h30m: if no signal, promote to 100%
T+4h: post-promote automation run and light regression test set (synthesis requests)
T+24h: day-1 retro: collect incident/alert logs, summarize anomalies

Canary guardrails (immediate abort triggers):
- Error rate delta > 3x baseline AND >0.5% absolute increase over 15m
- P50 latency > baseline + 200ms sustained for 10m
- P95 latency degradation > 500ms for 5m
- Elevated token-drop / model truncation errors observed in logs
- New uncaught exceptions with >10 occurrences in 5m
If any guardrail trips: immediate rollback to previous variant and notify #release-snackpack

Smoke test snippets (copy-pasteable):
1) Simple generation smoke (synthetic):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' -d '{"prompt": "Summarize: The new logging layer introduced. Output max 40 tokens."}'
Expect: 200, response length 15–60 tokens, no error field

2) Chat path sample (stateful):
Send 3-turn conversation that exercises KV cache (long context seed) and verify coherent reply within 2s median

3) Edge-case prompt for safety gating:
Input a prompt known to have produced a safety fallback previously; confirm expected safety signal and no crash

Telemetry watchboard (minimum tiles):
- Route level throttles (per-minute)
- Error-rate delta with moving baseline (1h)
- Token throughput (tokens/s) & cost-estimate delta
- Latency histogram: p50/p90/p95/p99 (1m granularity)
- Backend queue depth & GPU utilization (for Dedicated lanes)
- Canary-specific trace sample list (link to distributed traces)

Alert thresholds & who to call:
- P95 latency spike beyond threshold: Page SRE (Rina) -> Slack @channel -> evaluate
- Error-rate triple: Page Release lead (Aisha) and Ops liaison (Diego)
- Persistent model crash: Page Research/Applied ML on-call (alias: ml-oncall)

Rollback ladder (fastest-first):
1) Immediate variant flip (config-level rollback) -> reduces to previous model binary (a single command, tested)
2) Throttle to safe-level (reduce traffic to 0% for variant) + banlist if required
3) Full deploy of previous stable bundle if variant flip fails
4) Cascade to regional fallback (route blue/green)
Notes: practice variant flip in staging once per quarter. Documented commands below in the ops repo (linked artifact).

Operator quick commands (examples):
- Promote to percent: ./deployctl promote --route chat-v2 --variant canary --percent 20
- Flip to stable: ./deployctl switch --route chat-v2 --variant stable --instant
- Force rollback: ./deployctl rollback --route chat-v2 --to-tag v2026-09-21
- Fetch last 100 canary traces: ./telefetch traces --route chat-v2 --variant canary --limit 100

Post-release checklist (first 48h):
- [ ] Collect and snapshot logs for canary period (T+0 to T+4h)
- [ ] Run regression eval set (coverage prompts) and compare quality metrics to baseline
- [ ] Cost delta analysis (token/unit economics) — tag report to release PR
- [ ] Customer-facing release note finalization and publish
- [ ] Close release ticket and update changelog

Draft release notes (for commit to CHANGELOG and customer note):
Title: Oct 2026: Smarter routing + cold-cache warmup improvements
Summary: This release improves request routing heuristics and adds an adaptive cold-cache warmup to reduce tail latency on low-frequency routes. It also includes minor API ergonomics updates to the generate endpoint.
Highlights:
- Adaptive cache warmup reduces P95 latency on cold routes by ~20% in internal perf runs
- Model routing now prefers lower-cost variants when latency margin > 150ms (config opt-in)
- generate endpoint: added optional param `response_ttl` for short-lived caching behavior
Impact & migration notes:
- No breaking API changes. `response_ttl` is optional and safe to ignore.
- Customers on Dedicated may see slightly different routing behavior if they opt into cost-aware routing. We will surface the change in the dedicated-console rollout guide.
Known issues (short):
- Small subset of long-context prompts may observe slightly different completions due to cache-warmup ordering. We are tracking this in REL-2154.

Communication plan (internal -> external):
- T-60m: Internal email to stakeholders with watchboard link + escalation ladder
- T+2h: Short status update in #release-snackpack (ops brief)
- T+6h: If at 100% for 4h with no issues: draft customer note and send to legal/comm for review
- T+24h: Publish customer release note and changelog entry (Connor)

Retrospective prompts (postmortem template):
- What went well?
- Which guardrails triggered or almost triggered and why?
- Did our telemetry surface the right signals fast enough?
- Any surprising customer impacts or regressions?
- Action items (owner + due date)

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Decide default canary percent increments for weeknight releases (ops proposal due 2026-11-01)
- Add an automated synthetic that reproduces the long-context anomaly (assigned: Applied ML)
- Confirm deployctl command aliases exist in production operator shells (Connor to verify)

Quick references:
- Deploy commands & runbook in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/tree/main/deployctl
- Canary eval harness: CONF-8891
- Rollout ticket: REL-2154

Notes to self (handy reminders):
- Keep the Slack channel focused: pin the checklist and the watchboard link.
- If you reduce telemetry retention temporarily for noise suppression, remember to re-enable at T+6h.
- During the 50->100 step, consider a 15m hold if traffic patterns show spike risk (customer campaign windows).

-- end of snackpack draft --

Editorial: this doc is intentionally compact so on-call operators can scan and act. Treat as living: copy to dedicated-release lane and expand region-specific steps when cross-region deployment is required.
